# Review — PR 467 @ 91b6dad3d200

VERDICT: CHANGES_REQUESTED (code=CHANGES_REQUESTED, prose=n/a)

Posted by `local/bin/review.sh` at 2026-09-12T04:29:42Z — the local replacement for the `code-review` and `prose-review` jobs of `.github/workflows/pr-review.yml`.

Branch `issue-464-consistency-discarded-mass` onto `issue-422-pointwise-consistency-unit-bound`; merge base `a47b5661052192f739d5c6d12b14d9a7338b9e82`; head `91b6dad3d200d59f205fbbb546d878e529a8729a`.

## Findings

Checkbox states: `[ ]` unresolved (blocks the merge), `[x]` resolved.
Resolve a finding by ticking its box in this review body.

<!-- findings:begin -->
- [ ] F1 (changes) `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines.lean:3` — Remove the redundant `RestrictedAverage` import, already supplied by `RestrictedConsistency`.  <!-- lane=code -->
<!-- findings:end -->

## Code review

F1 requires changes under the requested import-hygiene criterion. `RestrictedConsistency.lean:2` already imports `MIPStarRE.QPBT.Games.RestrictedAverage`. Removing the duplicate import from the input stream leaves `Lines.lean` type-checking successfully, with identical existing proof-hole warnings.

The mathematics is sound. The average decomposition retains the conditional average’s mass multiplier and the entire discarded mass. `consistencyDefect_le_restrict_add_discarded_mass` derives the pointwise unit bound from complete measurements on opposite placements. Positive retained mass legitimately ensures conditioning is defined.

The new declarations explicitly identify themselves as auxiliary estimates supporting `lem:qld-xz-lines`, cited at `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:950–963`. The paper-facing statements and their blueprint counterparts remain unchanged.

All three changed Lean files type-check. All four new theorems depend only on `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`. The seven existing `sorry` warnings in `Lines.lean` remain; this PR does not complete that construction. I did not rerun full CI. The external `lean-conventions` skill was unavailable; I used the checked-in proof-integrity rules and project conventions.

# Review - PR 467 @ 025e6b5380df953ce8c80ff638fae64afcb45610

Independent review by a Claude Opus helper (owner-authorized 2026-09-17); no author, fixer or prior reviewer context reused. Trusted prompt, persona and policy ref: 92b252ed4bb1860b12a0a6c96084512f53ae9e10. Small proof packet for issue 464: one new 62-line Lean module carrying a single generic finite-conditioning estimate, one aggregator import line, and a scope brief.

## Findings

- none

## Review

**Base used.** The PR base `issue-422-pointwise-consistency-unit-bound` is already an ancestor of `github/main`, so the diff against the base merge base (8fc1b718, 188 files) is dominated by material that has since landed on main and is not this PR's content. I reviewed the main-relative change, `git diff 13409f63dea11a0e8a2f5d336215175448d4fccd 025e6b53`: four files, +133/-12. Worktree HEAD equals the published head, so no divergence adjustment was needed. Trusted policy (`local/personas/reviewer.md`, `local/personas/prose-reviewer.md`, `local/protocols/review.md`, `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` section 5, the `AGENTS.md` proof-integrity and Faithful Formalization sections) was read from `github/main` at 92b252ed; main advanced to cc3619b9 during the review, which does not affect the policy texts I used.

**Net content at merge.** `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Games/RestrictedAverage.lean` at this head is byte-identical to `github/main` (that half came in with the merged commit 73ebd926 from PR 433), so it contributes nothing on merge. The PR's own remaining contribution is `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/RestrictedConsistency.lean`, the import at `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines.lean:9`, and `local/briefs/464-consistency-discarded-mass.md`.

**Mathematics.** `consistencyDefect_le_restrict_add_discarded_mass` is correct and essentially tight. `avgOver` unfolds to a sum over the support; splitting it with `Finset.sum_filter_add_sum_filter_not` gives the good part, which `avgOver_restrict_mul_mass` identifies with the retained mass times the conditional average, plus the discarded part, where the only slack is replacing the integrand by 1 on the discarded set. The unit bound on that integrand is supplied by `consistencyDefect_integrand_le_one` (`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/PointwiseDefect.lean:28`), which derives it from completeness of the two `Measurement` families and `S.place_comm` under `hopp`, not from any assumed bound on the defect itself, so the docstring claim on that point is accurate. `hpos` is the boundary condition required for `Distribution.restrict` to be defined, not a trivializing hypothesis; there is no A1 conclusion-shaped hypothesis, no A3 zero-fallback, no A4 default witness, no `:= rfl` sleight of hand. The bound is in the useful direction (it restores the ambient defect rather than assuming it), and nothing here weakens a paper-labelled statement: both new declarations are explicitly formalization-only auxiliaries, carry no blueprint node, and cite `lem:qld-xz-lines` with the paper locator `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:950-963`, which I checked resolves to the pasting-lemma step of that proof. The brief's source-boundary and exclusion statements match what the code actually does.

**Duplication check.** I grepped `github/main` before accepting the new helper. No generic `consistencyDefect` conditioning lemma exists there; `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/Conditioning.lean:145-165` carries out the same derivation inline, specialized to `nondegenerateLinePastingDist` and its zero-direction discard bound. The new lemma is therefore a genuine generalization rather than a duplicate declaration, but it is unused at this head, and the natural follow-up is to have that `Conditioning.lean` passage call it instead of repeating the argument. That is a refactor for a later packet, not a merge blocker.

**Prior review.** The only earlier marked review is at head 91b6dad3 (CHANGES_REQUESTED, one unchecked finding). Its F1 asked to drop `import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Games.RestrictedAverage` from `Lines.lean` as redundant once `Lines.RestrictedConsistency` is imported. It is still unfixed at this head: `Lines.lean:10` still carries that import, `Lines.lean` uses no declaration from that module directly, and the import is now transitively supplied through line 9, so the observation is factually right. I do not carry it as a blocker. The import is pre-existing context in the diff rather than something this PR introduces, `AGENTS.md` section Imports pairs "prefer the smallest correct import set" with "do not churn imports unnecessarily", and the trusted severity ladder classes import churn as S2, for which `local/personas/reviewer.md` prescribes COMMENTED rather than CHANGES_REQUESTED. Recording it here so the disposition is explicit and reversible rather than silently dropped.

**Checks run.** `lake env lean MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/RestrictedConsistency.lean` in the PR worktree exits 0 with no diagnostics. Neither changed Lean file contains `sorry`, `admit`, `axiom` or `native_decide`. Exact-head CI is green on every gating context: `local-ci/build`, `blueprint-render`, `blueprint-sync`, `paper-gaps`, `file-length`, `proof-debt`, `proof-evasion`, `statement-origin`, and the `local-ci/summary` roll-up. The failing `local-review/summary` is the review slot this review fills, not a code defect. The PR reports mergeable with Motivation, Description and Testing sections present, and the one substantive commit follows `type(scope): short description`.

**Not checked.** I did not run a full `lake build` (machine-wide serialization) and rely on the exact-head `local-ci/build` status for whole-project elaboration; I did not re-verify the pre-existing proof holes in `Lines.lean`, which this PR neither adds to nor removes; I did not audit the 184 files that appear only in the base-relative diff because they are already on main; and I did not re-derive `DistanceCalculus.point_defect_eq`, taking the previously merged `PointwiseDefect.lean` as given.

Prose is n/a: the main-relative diff touches no blueprint TeX, paper-gap note or audit. The one Markdown file is a process brief, which I read for source-boundary accuracy.

VERDICT: APPROVED (code=APPROVED, prose=n/a)
